title: DIY Herb‑Spiced Oil for a Summer Barbecue Using Five‑Blade Scissors
meta_description: Learn how to make a vibrant herb‑spiced oil for summer barbecues using five‑blade Herb Scissors—quick, fresh flavor in every bite!
html:
When the grill fires up, a splash of herb spiced oil barbecue can turn ordinary meat, veggies, and even popcorn shrimp into a flavor‑packed masterpiece. The secret? Fresh herbs finely minced in a single snip with five‑blade Herb Scissors, then blended into a light oil that absorbs heat quickly and spreads evenly. This guide walks you through creating a versatile herb‑spiced oil that’s ready for any summer cook‑out.

Why a Herb‑Spiced Oil Is a Barbecue Game‑Changer

Most marinades sit in the fridge for hours, but a herb‑spiced oil works on the spot. The oil carries the aromatic compounds of cilantro, chives, and basil straight to the surface of the food, where the heat of the grill releases them instantly. This means you get bright, herbaceous notes without overcooking the greens. Plus, oil helps prevent sticking and adds a glossy finish that looks as good as it tastes.

Gather Your Tools and Ingredients

Everything you need fits in a small kitchen drawer. Having the right tools—especially the Herb Scissors—makes the process faster and keeps the herbs from bruising.

  • 1/2 cup neutral oil (grapeseed, canola, or light olive oil)
  • 2 tbsp fresh cilantro leaves
  • 2 tbsp fresh chives, trimmed
  • 2 tbsp fresh basil leaves
  • 1 tsp lemon zest
  • 1 tsp sea salt
  • Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
  • Herb Scissors (five‑blade herb shears)
  • Small bowl, whisk, and a clean glass jar with a lid

Step‑by‑Step: Mincing Herbs with Five‑Blade Herb Scissors

Using regular kitchen scissors or a knife can crush delicate herbs, releasing bitter flavors. The Herb Scissors’ five blades slice through cilantro, chives, and basil simultaneously, producing uniform, fluffy pieces that blend seamlessly into oil.

  1. Rinse and dry. Pat the herbs dry with a paper towel. Excess water dilutes the oil and can cause splatter.
  2. Trim. Remove any thick stems from cilantro and basil; keep chive roots if they’re thin.
  3. Snip. Place the herbs in a small pile and run the Herb Scissors over them 3‑4 times, rotating the pile each pass. The result should be a fine, even crumble.
  4. Clean. Use the included cleaning comb to remove any stuck pieces from the blades—this keeps the scissors ready for the next batch.

Now you have a bowl of perfectly minced herbs, ready to transform your oil.

Mixing the Herb‑Spiced Oil

Combine the minced herbs with the oil while it’s still at room temperature. Warm oil (not hot) helps the herbs release their flavors without cooking them.

1. Pour the oil into a small bowl. 2. Add the minced herb mixture, lemon zest, sea salt, and black pepper. 3. Whisk vigorously for 20‑30 seconds until the mixture looks slightly emulsified. 4. Transfer the blend to a glass jar, seal tightly, and let it sit for at least 15 minutes before using.

For a deeper flavor, you can let the oil rest for up to an hour. The herbs will continue to infuse, and the lemon zest will brighten the profile.

Putting the Herb‑Spiced Oil to Work on the Grill

Here are three quick ways to use your herb spiced oil barbecue style:

  • Brush on meats. Lightly coat chicken breasts, steak strips, or pork chops just before they hit the grill. The oil helps the heat conduct evenly while the herbs create a fragrant crust.
  • Season vegetables. Toss sliced zucchini, corn on the cob, or bell pepper strips in the oil before grilling. The herbs add a fresh lift that pairs beautifully with charred sweetness.
  • Finish drizzle. After removing food from the grill, drizzle a spoonful over the top for an immediate burst of brightness—perfect for shrimp skewers or grilled tofu.

Because the oil is already infused, you won’t need extra marinades or sauces, keeping your grill clean and your flavors pure.

Storing and Reusing Your Herb‑Spiced Oil

Herb‑spiced oil stays vibrant for up to a week in the refrigerator. Keep it in a dark glass jar to protect the herbs from light, which can degrade flavor. Before each use, give the jar a quick shake—some herbs may settle at the bottom. If you notice any off smell or cloudiness, discard it; fresh herbs are best used quickly for peak taste.

FAQ

Can I substitute other herbs?

Absolutely. Try mint for a cooling note, or rosemary for a piney depth. The Herb Scissors work best with soft herbs, so avoid overly woody stems.

Is it safe to use the herb‑spiced oil on a hot grill?

Yes, but apply it in a thin layer. The oil’s flash point is higher than most cooking oils, and the herbs won’t burn unless left on the grill for an extended time.

Do I need to wash the Herb Scissors after each use?

Rinse them under warm water, then use the cleaning comb to dislodge any remaining bits. A quick dry prevents rust and keeps the blades sharp for your next barbecue.
